pr_title: Add checkbox to delete pull branch after successful merge
pr_comments:
Sometimes these errors are logged:

```
2021/06/02 09:12:34 ...es/pull/temp_repo.go:144:createTemporaryRepo() [E] Unable to fetch head_repo head branch [jpraet/test:jpraet-patch-2 -> tracking in C:\gitea\data\tmp\local-repo\pull.git592031210]: exit status 128:

        fatal: Couldn't find remote ref refs/heads/jpraet-patch-2

2021/06/02 09:12:34 ...vices/pull/update.go:91:GetDiverging() [E] CreateTemporaryPath: Unable to fetch head_repo head branch [jpraet/test:jpraet-patch-2 -> tracking in tmpBasePath]: exit status 128

        fatal: Couldn't find remote ref refs/heads/jpraet-patch-2

2021/06/02 09:12:34 ...ervices/pull/pull.go:305:func1() [E] GetDiverging: Unable to fetch head_repo head branch [jpraet/test:jpraet-patch-2 -> tracking in tmpBasePath]: exit status 128

        fatal: Couldn't find remote ref refs/heads/jpraet-patch-2

```

When a PR gets merged, a TestPullRequest task is scheduled asynchrounously:

https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/blob/894742278154781ba4cb347ac4c7efd7d6dcd1c8/services/pull/merge.go#L55

If the branch gets deleted before this task has completed, you will get these errors in the logs.

What is the purpose of this task?

It looks like it's not the task scheduled from merge.go that is causing the problem, because if the PR was successfully merged that one doesn't do anything.

The problematic one is scheduled here:

https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/blob/6a7bf974bef6257517e39d9979b4ebac8c35176a/services/repository/push.go#L141

as a result of the push to the target branch, which happens before the PR is marked as merged.

Yes it works fine functionally, but the errors in the logs are unpleasant. I made a change to detect this scenario and log it as a warning instead of error, not sure if that's the right approach?

```
2021/06/03 22:38:35 ...ervices/pull/pull.go:306:func1() [W] Cannot test PR my-repo/45: head_branch jpraet-patch-1 no longer exists
```

When delete a branch, gitea should close all related PRs, then the check will not continue and the error log will not occur.

So I think this is a bug of `DeleteBranch` we haven't found before. It should close all related opened PRs.

UPDATE:

I sent #16067 to fix the bug.

> 
> UPDATE:
> 
> I sent #16067 to fix the bug.

I don't think that's the problem here. The PR is already marked as merged and closed before I call `CleanupPullRequest()`. And as I commented in your PR: it looks like `CloseBranchPulls()` is already being called when deleting a branch.

As far as I can tell the issue is the asynchronous `AddTestPullRequestTask` goroutine that is automatically scheduled when the merge commit is pushed to the target branch. While that task is running, we are deleting the branch.
Should this also be supported through the API? To me, it seems like this compound operation of merging a PR and also deleting the source branch mainly makes sense as a UI convenience.
It's OK from me to allow API to do that.

issue_context.title: Automatic Deletion of Unprotected branches on PR merge with toggleable switch
issue_context.body:
- Gitea version (or commit ref): 1.14.0+dev-208-g6280af032
- Git version: 2.29.0
- Operating system: Linux Ubuntu 16.04
- Database (use `[x]`):
  - [ ] PostgreSQL
  - [x] MySQL
  - [ ] MSSQL
  - [ ] SQLite
- Can you reproduce the bug at https://try.gitea.io:
  - [ ] Yes (provide example URL)
  - [x] No (not a bug.)
- Log gist:

## Description

* Toggleable switch at project level for use
* if an **unprotected** branch is merged while switch is set to true, that branch gets deleted
* protected branches are unaffected

## Screenshots
comments: I think merge option will get to overloaded, should we make this a user and/or repo setting?

Yes I intended it to be togglable in the repo's own settings. I don't user repos that often, I considered one at organization level, because I will be personally enabling them in most of our projects but figured it would be too annoying to have 3 options of 'organization default', on, off

Assume the situations:

- [ ] The branch is a default branch on the same repository, send PRs from default branch to non-default branch.
- [ ] The branch is a default branch on the forked repository.
- [ ] The branch on forked repository has also been sent to another upstream and one PR merged but another not.
- [ ] There are also some PRs sent to the forked repository branch. I sent a PR from the branch of my forked repositories to original, and another forked repositories sent a PR to the branch. Then before I merge the PR on my forked repositories, the PR I sent to upstream has been merged.

> @lunny Can't forked repositories change the fork repo settings? I would have thought so…

@delvh You can, but if you have many forks, you may have to change every repository. Since the fork repositories is your copy of original repositories, so the settings depends on your personal usage habit.

A checkbox like this on the merge form could already be an easy win. Even if it would be disabled by default, at least it saves you from scrolling down to the bottom of the page, clicking the delete branch button and the confirmation dialog. And it serves as a reminder too.

![afbeelding](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2212615/119569640-505b0180-bdaf-11eb-9b5b-e19cd67840f6.png)

Maybe the text could be `Delete head branch if not protected or default`.
I would prefere @jpraet way but hide it if the branch is protected ...
Or disable the checkbox and display the reason
